title: testing: ignore Cython's PyPy collection_type warning
body:
Written by Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code for the pytest maintainers; I prompted it, it did the work, I read it.

`main` has been red on `build (ubuntu-pypy3-xdist)` since the runners picked up PyPy 3.11.16 (PyPy 8.0.0). The failure is `testing/python/metafunc.py::TestMetafunc::test_idval_hypothesis`:

```
RuntimeWarning: cython.collection_type only works on PyPy with the C flag CYTHON_USE_TYPE_SPECS=1
numpy/random/_generator.pyx:1: RuntimeWarning
```

hypothesis imports `numpy.random` whenever numpy is already loaded. On PyPy 3.11.16, the Cython-compiled `_generator` module emits this warning on import, and our `filterwarnings = error` turns it into a test failure.

The last green run and the first red one differ only in PyPy (3.11.15 → 3.11.16) and hypothesis (6.168.0 → 6.168.1); numpy is 2.4.6 in both. On PyPy 3.11.15 with numpy 2.4.6 and hypothesis 6.168.1, `numpy.random` imports cleanly under `-W error`, so hypothesis is not the cause.

This adds one message-matched ignore to our warning filters. It only affects pytest's own test suite and changes nothing for users, so it has no changelog entry.

This also clears the same failure from every open PR's CI once they rebase.
